title: Rule Requiring Drivers of Public Service Vehicles to Ensure No Property Left Behind by Passengers Before or After Trip
what_it_is: Rule Requiring Drivers of Public Service Vehicles to Ensure No Property Left Behind by Passengers Before or After Trip

sections.label: LTA enforcement and review
sections.summary: LTA has issued only warnings, withdrew one warning after appeals, and is reviewing best practices for P2P drivers with partners.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: LTA has only issued warnings in a few instances and has not imposed any financial penalties or demerit points on drivers for non-compliance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The warning recently issued to a driver for breaching this rule has been withdrawn, following appeals to LTA through the driver's Member of Parliament and the National Taxi Association.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: LTA will take this opportunity to not only review how this best practice should be encouraged to protect the interests of both drivers and their passengers, but also conduct a broader review of best practices for P2P drivers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: LTA is, thus, working with our tripartite partners, our P2P operators and the driver associations to undertake this review, taking into consideration recent public feedback and will share the outcome of the review when ready.

sections.label: Driver concerns and public education
sections.summary: Associations raised concerns about checking for left belongings, and LTA will consider reminders and public education with operators and associations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Our driving community at the National Taxi Association and the National Private Hire Vehicles Association had expressed their concerns over the practical realities of being able to check, with absolute certainty, whether a passenger had left their belongings in the cars when they alight.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: And I am very glad that LTA will consider relooking at this rule on punitive actions against our drivers if they have not done so.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, given this and the feedback that the drivers have given, will LTA also look at joint public education campaigns, letting our drivers and passengers know that it is a joint effort on belongings that are left behind and also to work with more of the taxi and private hire platforms on ensuring that there are reminders, whether it is on the app or in the taxis via stickers and all that, on reminding people not to leave their items behind?

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Certainly, we will work together with our P2P operators as well as the associations to look at how we can remind drivers as well as passengers to take some responsibility, in terms of stewardship of the vehicles as well as responsibility for their personal belongings through notices or apps and so on.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: And just to share with Members too – besides teaching the drivers this practice during their Vocational Licence training course, they are also reminded of this practice when they undergo their refresher course.
